items.title: Cortex-M3 event register omission
items.condition: Interrupt pending before WFE may miss an event.
items.handling: The reviewed software slice offers no WFE low-power policy.

items.title: Flash read after WFI or WFE
items.condition: Sleep may disrupt reads when using two wait states and prefetch with the Flash interface clock gated.
items.handling: HSI8 uses zero wait states. PLL72 retains the Flash interface gate. The dedicated HSI8 STOP mode keeps that gate open and issues WFI only.

items.title: DBGMCU debug registers inaccessible to user firmware
items.condition: Ordinary firmware may observe zero for DBGMCU_IDCODE and DBGMCU_CR.
items.handling: Flash-size halfword provides a capacity check. Physical revision and debug freeze belong to the external probe.

items.title: Debug STOP with pending SysTick
items.condition: Enabled SysTick interrupt during debug STOP wakes the system.
items.handling: The baremetal STOP owner admits only idle SysTick and no pending tick.

items.title: Debug STOP with WFE
items.condition: Sequential instructions after WFE can be skipped with debug STOP enabled.
items.handling: The dedicated falling-edge interrupt owner only enters WFI.

items.title: LSE startup in harsh environments
items.condition: The crystal can fail to start on first backup domain power-on in harsh environments.
items.handling: The adopted route requires a running LSE and fresh APB synchronization. Explicit provisioning bounds failure by time and polls, retains an already selected clock and leaves backup data intact. Crystal startup margin, VBAT retention and the field PCB workaround require hardware qualification.

items.title: PVD and USB wakeup events
items.condition: A PVD EXTI event cannot wake the core from WFE-based sleep as described.
items.handling: The maintained HSI8 PVD route reads the comparator level through PWR only. It admits no IRQ, event wake or millivolt claim.

items.title: Flash memory BSY latency after STRT
items.condition: BSY can read clear on the first bus cycle after starting page erase.
items.handling: Complete and read back the control write before polling status. The controller then requires EOP without an error flag and verifies the page.

items.title: LSI clock stabilization time
items.condition: The oscillator can remain outside the specified frequency range after LSIRDY asserts.
items.handling: Wait 128 nominal microseconds after LSIRDY on the selected HSI8 timebase. Observe an owned clock request and settle it before irreversible activation.

items.title: USART1 RTS and CAN TX alternate output
items.condition: PA12 has its CAN TX path selected when CAN is not clocked but USART1 is.
items.handling: The reference Board claims PA12, requires CAN remap 00 and rejects a foreign active USART1 before changing pads. The transceiver stays disabled until CAN and routing acknowledge.

items.title: SPI1 slave and USART2 synchronous clock
items.condition: With both peripheral clocks enabled, SPI1 slave disables USART2 CK on alternate-function PA4. No silicon workaround is given.
items.handling: SPI1 admits only master polling and configures PA4 as a software GPIO chip select. The synchronous USART2 route exclusively claims SPI1. Cold admission rejects a boot-enabled SPI1 clock before modifying pads or USART configuration.

items.title: SPI1 master and USART2 synchronous clock
items.condition: With both peripheral clocks enabled, SPI1 master using software NSS prevents USART2 CK on PA4. The documented workaround changes SPI1 SSOE.
items.handling: The SPI1 endpoint leases PA4 as GPIO output. Its synchronous USART2 alternate-function mode is outside the selected assembly. The synchronous USART2 route exclusively claims SPI1. Cold admission rejects a boot-enabled SPI1 clock before modifying pads or USART configuration.

items.title: SPI2 master and USART3 synchronous clock
items.condition: SPI2 software NSS prevents the synchronous USART3 clock on PB12.
items.handling: The short-poll profile uses PB12 as software CS. No USART3 synchronous controller is admitted.

items.title: I2C2 SMBA and SPI2 NSS share PB12
items.condition: I2C2 enabled can take ownership of PB12 when it is an alternate function output.
items.handling: SPI2 uses a GPIO software CS. The fixture selects I2C1 and no I2C2 controller.

items.title: Remapped SPI1 master and I2C1 SMBA conflict
items.condition: Remapped SPI1 PB5 MOSI conflicts with I2C1 SMBA when both peripheral clocks are on.
items.handling: The default SPI1 route requires remap bit zero both in configuration and hardware. A preexisting remap rejects before claiming the SPI1 clock or pads.

items.title: I2C1 and TIM3_CH2 remapped
items.condition: Partial TIM3 remap makes alternate output PB5 contend with I2C1 SMBA.
items.handling: Quadrature uses the default PA6/PA7 route with both phases as inputs. The cold admission reads and rejects nondefault TIM3 remap.

items.title: DMA channel disable and transfer error when clearing the global flag
items.condition: A simultaneous transfer error and whole-channel flag clear may leave the channel enabled and hide TEIF.
items.handling: Withdraw the USART DMA request, disable and verify the channel, inspect late TEIF, then clear individual TCIF, HTIF and TEIF flags with an aligned 32-bit IFCR write. Section 2.4.2 requires aligned 32-bit DMA register accesses.

items.title: ADC1 injected conversion can disturb PA0
items.condition: Injected operation can couple a voltage glitch to ADC input 0.
items.handling: The reviewed ADC1 PA0 path uses regular single-shot conversions only, with JEXTTRIG and injected auto conversion disabled.

items.title: Automatic PWM output can reenable after system break
items.condition: Automatic output enable can reassert MOE after loss of a system break condition.
items.handling: Keep AOE zero, require explicit recovery with outputs off and recheck BKIN and BIF before and after the separate start.

items.title: Consecutive compare events may be missed
items.condition: Consecutive compare events can be lost in toggle mode or center-aligned compare interrupts.
items.handling: Periodic PWM uses PWM1 and the fixed one-pulse route uses PWM2 with an unchanged CCR while running. No compare interrupts, toggle output or compare triggers are published.

items.title: External timer counter reset and OCREF clear
items.condition: External counter reset can extend the inactive PWM interval with OCREF clear.
items.handling: TIM3 CH1 fixed PWM and one-pulse routes have no slave reset or OCREF clear path.

items.title: Missing capture flag
items.condition: An edge concurrent with a CCR1 read may clear CC1IF without setting CC1OF.
items.handling: Use the PB6 EXTI6 witness around the CCR1 read. Keep its shared NVIC vector disabled and report observed loss without estimating a physical edge count. The TIM3 encoder reads CNT only and never consumes CCR or capture flags.

items.title: Overcapture detected too early
items.condition: CC1OF can report overcapture although both samples were retained.
items.handling: Treat the hardware flag as an observable incident; the public capture API does not promise an exact count of lost edges.

items.title: General timer 100 percent PWM after OCREF clear
items.condition: An OCREF clear action can suppress full duty indefinitely.
items.handling: TIM3 CH1 fixed PWM does not enable OCREF clear, and every admitted full-duty value fits in CCR1.

items.title: RVU remains set at low APB clock frequency
items.condition: An APB frequency below twice the IWDG clock can prevent the reload update flag from clearing.
items.handling: Admit the live HSI8 / APB1 8 MHz clock before activation. Bound the RVU wait and retain the irreversible owner on failure.

items.title: PVU remains set at low APB clock frequency
items.condition: An APB frequency below twice the IWDG clock can prevent the prescaler update flag from clearing.
items.handling: Require the same reviewed APB1 clock and wait for both PVU and RVU before verifying the nominal settings.

items.title: RVU and PVU remain set in Stop mode
items.condition: Entering Stop immediately after updating the watchdog registers can leave update flags pending.
items.handling: Wait for both shadow flags in Run and retain irreversible effects on failure. This mode does not expose Stop.

items.title: I2C byte events must precede the next transfer
items.condition: Late software handling can duplicate, miss or introduce bytes.
items.handling: Hold SCL where ACK/STOP ordering requires a dedicated window and wait for BTF for longer reads and controller writes. I2C1 target receive rejects a missed EV2 window. Target modes keep stretching enabled. The combined target mode requires a drained RX phase before its second local match. Transmit feeds one byte on EV1, then waits for BTF or terminal AF.

items.title: I2C receive data may corrupt around STOP
items.condition: Delayed final DR reads can corrupt the final received byte.
items.handling: The two-byte and longer receive paths hold SCL across the critical DR/STOP sequence.

items.title: SMBus cannot always NACK an invalid payload
items.condition: The hardware cannot satisfy every SMBus v2.0 acknowledgment contract.
items.handling: The admitted mode is I2C master polling with separate seven- and ten-bit endpoints. SMBus is outside this mode.

items.title: Misplaced I2C STOP inhibits a new START
items.condition: A misplaced STOP can stall SB detection or make an attempted START report BERR.
items.handling: Bound the wait for SB. A failed pending START enters a local reset using CR1.SWRST; the owner must explicitly recover.

items.title: I2C repeated START timing at 88 to 100 kHz
items.condition: Master standard mode can violate repeated START setup when a target stretches or the SCL rise exceeds the rated margin.
items.handling: Admit the exact nominal 80 kHz HSI8 profile, with APB1-8MHz CR2 FREQ 8, CCR 50 and TRISE 9.

items.title: I2C slave data valid time can be late
items.condition: Slave transmit with no clock stretching can miss data timing without OVR.
items.handling: I2C1 has separately selected receive-only and transmit-only targets. Transmit keeps NOSTRETCH clear and does not prefetch in TXE. The peer must accept clock stretching.

items.title: Analog I2C filters can hold BUSY after local reset
items.condition: A stuck analog filter needs externally safe electrical transitions before reset can clear BUSY.
items.handling: Local recovery uses CR1.SWRST and verified idle lines. Persistent BUSY remains an error; this fixture does not issue unqualified GPIO recovery pulses.

items.title: Early clearing of the parity error flag
items.condition: Reading DR before RXNE can leave a parity error reasserting until the stop bit.
items.handling: Smartcard disables the independent parity interrupt and waits for RXNE before reading DR. A pending early PE blocks a queued data-register write.

items.title: USART idle frame detection at receiver clock deviation
items.condition: Clock mismatch can prevent detection of IDLE.
items.handling: The initial USART2 mode owns a byte IRQ ring; it does not depend on IDLE or promise gap timing. Finite DMA reports observed IDLE as advisory and also retires on full count or caller-owned stop.

items.title: USART transmit can clear receiver parity error
items.condition: With parity enabled in full duplex, a data-register write can clear the receiver PE flag.
items.handling: The initial 8N1 mode has no parity. The Smartcard owner serializes one TX character, preserves pending PE without RXNE, and observes complete RX before writing DR. Simultaneous USART2 DMA remains 8N1; its IRQ only observes RX/TX status. Concurrent full-duplex parity behavior remains a silicon limit.

items.title: Break transmission disregards nCTS
items.condition: A requested hardware break can transmit without the peer asserting nCTS.
items.handling: RTS/CTS accepts byte requests only. The separate LIN personality leaves CTSE disabled.

items.title: An RTS protocol violation can assert ready while RDR is full
items.condition: The partner sends another frame while nRTS is inactive and the earlier RDR word is unconsumed.
items.handling: The IRQ parks PA1 inactive before reading DR after ORE or before using the last event slot. It preserves the ordered receive prefix and reports lost data. Behavior before the ISR observes the violation remains a physical limitation.

items.title: SPI slave CRC may accumulate even with NSS high
items.condition: The SPI slave CRC can observe the shared clock while the slave is unselected.
items.handling: This mode selects controller polling without hardware CRC or slave operation.

items.title: SPI CRC is sensitive to another device on the same DMA channel
items.condition: Simultaneous DMA traffic on a shared request channel can corrupt SPI CRC.
items.handling: SPI1 and SPI2 short-poll use no DMA requests or hardware CRC. SPI2 finite DMA has CRCEN disabled and exclusively leases both wired channels.

items.title: bxCAN time-triggered communication mode not supported
items.condition: The CAN_MCR TTCM bit must remain clear. Hardware time-triggered timestamps are unavailable.
items.handling: Fixed internal silent loopback leaves TTCM clear and timestamps the event when the task consumes the FIFO.

items.title: False wakeup due to an old K state
items.condition: A pending RESUME signal can survive until FSUSP and raise WKUP early.
items.handling: Self-powered reference retains all clocks and makes no suspend-current claim. LP service distinguishes sampled J, K and SE0. It does not use a forced reset as a power workaround.

items.title: ESOF desynchronization after local resume signaling
items.condition: Locally driven resume may generate a premature suspend.
items.handling: The selected PMA face has no local remote wakeup/RESUME method.

items.title: Software cannot use the received CRC16 bytes
items.condition: Stored CRC bytes can be corrupted although hardware verification still works.
items.handling: PMA reads only the validated payload count. Wire CRC bytes are not exposed.

items.title: Incorrect full-packet RX count with slow APB1
items.condition: Exactly full OUT packets can report one byte less if APB1 is below 13 MHz.
items.handling: Selected exact PLL supplies 36 MHz APB1 and the cold C lease rejects a different divider. The selected EP1 shares the same bounded APB1 and exact 64-byte PMA block.

items.title: USART TX pin remains owned during receive-only use

items.title: Flash memory BSY latency after STRT
items.condition: The first status read after STRT can precede the BSY assertion.
items.handling: Read back the control register before polling BSY, require a fresh EOP and verify the selected 2 KiB single-bank page.

items.title: SDIO with TIM8
items.condition: TIM8_CH4 output conflicts with SDIO in 1-bit and 4-bit modes.
items.handling: Reserve PC9 even in 1-bit mode and reject inherited alternate output mode during cold prepare. TIM8 exposes only CH1 and rejects configurations enabling other channels.

items.title: SDIO and TIM3 remap
items.condition: Fully remapped TIM3_CH4 output conflicts with SDIO_D1.
items.handling: Reserve PC9 for the entire SDIO lease.

items.title: SDIO with USART3 and UART4
items.condition: Partially remapped USART3_TX and UART4_TX conflict with SDIO_D2 in 1-bit mode.
items.handling: Reserve PC10 for the entire SDIO lease and reject inherited alternate output mode.

items.title: I2S2 WS conflicts with synchronous USART3 CK after use
items.condition: A previously used I2S2 can still drive PB12 in alternate-function output after its clock is gated.
items.handling: Synchronous USART3 is outside this assembly. A future owner transition requires the ES0340 SPI2 reset after clock withdrawal.

items.title: USART TX pin remains owned during receive-only use
items.condition: When the USART is enabled, clearing TE can still hold the alternate-function TX line high.
items.handling: The reviewed USART2 mode owns both TX and RX for the whole activation; an alternate driver cannot take PA2 from it.

items.title: DMA global flag clear can lose an active transfer error
items.condition: CGIFx writes clear all flags and may lose an error during a live channel transfer.
items.handling: Only the channel's individual HTIF, TCIF and TEIF W1C bits are written. DMA register accesses are aligned 32-bit words.

items.title: PA0 disturbance during injected conversion
items.condition: Any injected sequence can couple a disturbance to PA0.
items.handling: Only regular simultaneous external PA1 and PA2 are admitted. No injected trigger or PA0 acquisition is configured.

items.title: Automatic output can re-enable after a system break
items.condition: An AOE-controlled cycle can automatically rearm after a system break.
items.handling: AOE remains clear so only explicit software start can arm MOE.

items.title: Consecutive compare event can be missed
items.condition: Toggle output and center-aligned compare event sequences can miss an event.
items.handling: Use edge-aligned PWM1 without a compare event consumer.

items.title: Output compare clear may not follow external counter reset
items.condition: External reset can extend OCREF clear through an extra PWM period.
items.handling: No external reset mode and no OCREF clear function is selected.

items.title: USART idle frame detection at receiver clock deviation
items.condition: Clock mismatch can prevent detection of IDLE.
items.handling: The initial USART2 mode owns a byte IRQ ring; it does not depend on IDLE or promise gap timing.

items.title: USART transmit can clear receiver parity error
items.condition: With parity enabled in full duplex, a data-register write can clear the receiver PE flag.
items.handling: The initial USART2 mode uses 8N1. Production parity modes require a separate review.

items.title: SPI2 or I2S2 slave modes can assert TXE prematurely
items.condition: Cut Z can signal TXE twice before RXNE, corrupting transmitted data in slave modes.
items.handling: Only I2S2 master transmit is admitted; no slave DMA path is present.

items.title: PCM long frame synchronisation with 16-bit payload in 32-bit slot
items.condition: An I2S master using 16-bit data in a 32-bit PCM long slot generates WS every 16 bits.
items.handling: The software route admits Philips stereo 16-bit slots only.

items.title: I2S slave mode start requires a known WS level
items.condition: In slave mode starting at the wrong WS level can prevent proper synchronisation.
items.handling: SPI2 is owned exclusively by the finite I2S master-transmitter mode.

items.title: Slave mode synchronization can be lost on SCK or WS glitches
items.condition: A slave cannot detect loss of alignment after an unexpected edge.
items.handling: The selected master owns CK and WS and does not depend on external slave synchronization.

items.title: Limited multibyte I/O support
items.condition: SDIO I/O function transfer can fail.
items.handling: The selected mode uses SD memory CMD17 exclusively.

items.title: Hardware flow control corruption
items.condition: Hardware flow control may corrupt data.
items.handling: Clock control keeps HWFC_EN clear. The receiver verifies FIFO, CRC and timeout.

items.title: CRC-less response flags
items.condition: The controller may set CCRCFAIL for a response without CRC.
items.handling: Only OCR R3 accepts CCRCFAIL. Responses with CRC require controller CRC proof and applicable command index.

items.title: Negative clock edge corruption
items.condition: Negative edge clock mode may corrupt response or data.
items.handling: The fixed identification clock keeps NEGEDGE clear during the session.

items.title: CE-ATA busy management
items.condition: CE-ATA has a separate busy response hazard.
items.handling: The selected mode uses only the SD memory protocol.

items.title: Absent TX underrun evidence
items.condition: TX underrun may corrupt data without TXUNDERR when six parent cycles are at least one data-word transfer.
items.handling: Explicit CMD24 validates both 8 MHz parents and the divide-by-22 host. In four-line mode six parent cycles are 0.75 microseconds and one wire word lasts 22 microseconds. Both modes require the block CRC result and card readiness.

limitations: IWDG activation is reviewed under HSI8 only. Its board supply does not admit DS5319 Table 25 oscillator bounds, and this mode exposes no Stop path.
Source review covers GPIO, USART2 8N1 IRQ byte queue and opt-in halfword/page Flash under HSI8 or the reviewed 8 MHz MCO bypass and PLL72.
This audit indexes selected sections for the maintained slice; other ES096 sections and other F1 groups are not admitted by this profile.
No physical silicon cut, oscillator accuracy, board wiring, timings, DMA, remap, low-power or physical qualification is established.
Low-, high- and XL-density software references select GPIO output, USART2 IRQ and HSI8. Additional modes require their exact package and errata reviews.
F100, F101, F102, F105 and F107 exact software references select HSI8, GPIO output and USART2 IRQ byte events.
F100 high-density, F101 low/high/XL-density and F102 low-density software references select HSI8, GPIO output and USART2 IRQ byte events.
The exact F103RB HSI8 control slice uses TIM3 CH1 on PA6, ADC1 regular sampling of PA0, and EXTI13 PC13 IRQ events with the documented B1 wiring.
PVD polling on the exact F103RB HSI8 fixture supplies a raw threshold code and comparator state. Electrical trip points and wake behavior require separate qualification.
